The skill remains documentation-focused, but installation examples should be reviewed before use.

remediation.suggestion: Pin release URLs and provide checksum verification; explain that users must inspect downloaded binaries before execution.

remediation.issue: Documentation examples reference external sites and local configuration paths.

content.value_statement: Go projects often have incomplete comments, examples, and contributor guidance that slow adoption and maintenance. This skill provides structured guidance for writing, reviewing, and organizing documentation that matches Go conventions.
actual_capabilities: Draft package, type, function, and method comments that follow Go documentation conventions.
Create README, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, and llms.txt content for Go projects.
Design runnable Example test functions and Go Playground documentation links.
Adapt documentation guidance for libraries, applications, and command-line tools.
Review existing documentation for missing context, inaccurate claims, and weak structure.
limitations: It does not inspect a repository unless you provide the relevant files or excerpts.
It does not run Go tests, build binaries, or publish documentation.
Generated examples require review for API accuracy, security, and project-specific behavior.
It cannot replace maintainers decisions about compatibility, release policy, or supported environments.

use_cases.title: Document a Go library
use_cases.description: Generate package comments, API explanations, examples, and README sections from supplied Go declarations and behavior.

use_cases.title: Improve an application guide
use_cases.description: Organize setup, configuration, operations, architecture, and troubleshooting content for a Go service or CLI.

use_cases.title: Review a documentation change
use_cases.description: Assess comments, examples, contribution guidance, and release notes for clarity, completeness, and consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Start with a package comment
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a concise package comment for this Go package. Use only facts in the supplied code and state its main purpose.

prompt_templates.title: Build a README outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a README outline for this Go project using the supplied repository details. Include installation, quick start, configuration, usage, testing, and support sections.

prompt_templates.title: Add executable examples
prompt_templates.prompt: Write Go ExampleXxx test functions for the supplied public API. Include realistic inputs, expected output comments, and cases that clarify important behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit project documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the supplied Go project documentation as a maintainer. Identify unsupported claims, missing usage context, inconsistent terminology, and gaps across API docs, README, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, and CLI help. Propose precise revisions.

output_examples.input: A Go package with exported types and methods but sparse comments.
output_examples.output: A package overview, convention-compliant API comments, and focused examples that explain behavior and edge cases.

output_examples.input: A CLI repository needing onboarding and release documentation.
output: A contribution guide with local setup and validation steps
A changelog entry following the chosen release format

output_examples.input: A draft Example test and its expected output.
output_examples.output: A reviewed example with clearer naming, deterministic output, and documentation notes for users.

best_practices: Provide the relevant code and project facts, then ask for documentation grounded only in that evidence.
Prefer runnable, deterministic examples that show one important behavior at a time.
Review generated text with maintainers and run project checks before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not invent APIs, commands, configuration keys, versions, or compatibility claims.
Do not use generic comments that merely repeat an identifier without explaining behavior.
Do not copy installation commands or external links into production guidance without reviewing their source and safety.

faq.question: What kinds of Go documentation can this skill help create?
faq.answer: It covers godoc comments, README files, CONTRIBUTING guides, CHANGELOG entries, CLI help, examples, and llms.txt files.

faq.question: Can it document both libraries and applications?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the project type and relevant files so the guidance can address APIs or operational workflows.

faq.question: Does it generate runnable examples?
faq.answer: It can draft ExampleXxx test functions and Playground-oriented examples, but you must compile and test them.

faq.question: Can it review existing documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. Supply the document and its related code or project context for an evidence-based review.

faq.question: Does it publish or modify my repository?
faq.answer: No. It returns documentation guidance and drafts. You control edits, commands, reviews, and publication.

faq.question: How should I validate generated documentation?
faq.answer: Check claims against the code, run formatting and tests, verify links, and ask a maintainer to review project-specific details.
